raw_response:
Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-rays demonstrate marked tracheomegaly (dilated trachea) and extensive bilateral cystic/cavitary changes consistent with tracheobronchomegaly (Mounier-Kuhn syndrome). The progression to increased number and size of intrapulmonary cavities indicates disease advancement, for which management focuses on treating acute infections with antibiotics and airway clearance via physiotherapy.
